acceptance: Part payloads validate declared ranges, decompressed size, and target ownership before disk writes.
evidence: Normal and I64 part payloads validate file hash, range, length, file size, and peer-owned range. Compressed part chunks validate declared compressed size, stream ownership, output bounds, and retained flate2 inflation before exposing bytes to disk owners.
notes: Use flate2 only for compressed payloads.

acceptance: Stalled or cancelled requests send cancel where useful and release owned ranges.
evidence: Native cancel frame construction is covered. Peer transfer state releases owned ranges on timeout, remote cancel, corrupt block, and no-needed-parts transitions without busy loops.

acceptance: Bad packet, corrupt block, timeout, disconnect, and no-needed-parts map to bounded retry states.
evidence: Retriable failures enter bounded backoff, remote cancel and out-of-parts return to queue, no-file fails the peer, and no-needed-parts remains explicit for source policy.
